messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

function.name: get_average_monthly_temperature

message.content:
The “best” month really depends on what you’re looking for—weather, crowds, or price—but most travelers find that **late spring (April–June) and early fall (September–November)** offer the sweet spot.

| Season | Typical Weather | Crowds | Price |
|--------|-----------------|--------|-------|
| **Late Spring (Apr‑Jun)** | Warm (70–80 °F / 21–27 °C), lower humidity, occasional showers in May | Moderate – fewer tourists than peak summer | Mid‑range; prices start to rise in June |
| **Summer (Jul‑Aug)** | Hot (80–90 °F / 27–32 °C), high humidity, dry but can feel sticky | Peak season – crowded beaches, higher hotel rates | Highest prices, especially July & August |
| **Early Fall (Sep‑Oct)** | Warm (75–85 °F / 24–29 °C), drier after monsoon season ends | Moderate – crowds thin out after Labor Day | Prices drop after mid‑August, but still decent |
| **Winter (Nov‑Feb)** | Mild (60–70 °F / 15–21 °C), rainy in some areas, cooler at night | Low crowds, great deals | Lowest prices, but more rain in December‑January |

**Bottom line:** If you want sunny skies with fewer crowds and reasonable rates, aim for **May, September, or October**. If you’re okay with higher prices and don’t mind the heat, July and August are fine for beach activities. And if you’re a budget traveler who doesn’t mind a bit of rain, late winter (March‑April) can also be a good time.
